*Speaking as the farmer...*

Alright, it's planting time again. Let me think about this year on my 6 mu.

I've been doing wheat-maize for a long time, my whole life really. Same 6 mu — wheat in the winter, maize in the summer, one right after the other. That's how everyone around here does it. No point trying something different when you've only got 6 mu. You change crops and get it wrong, you lose everything.

**Wheat first.** I'll plant around October 10th or 12th, same as always. Mid-October is when everybody around here puts wheat in. I buy seed at the agricultural supply shop in the town — a common variety, nothing fancy. My neighbor Old Wang tried one of those expensive new seeds two years ago and didn't get much more than me, so I stick with what I know. About 15 kg of seed per mu.

For fertilizer, I buy compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) — one bag is 40 kg, I put about one bag per mu down before planting when I till. Then when the wheat starts jointing in spring, I topdress with urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. That's what works. My wife says I'm stubborn about this but it's been fine for years. If I had more money I might put a little more, but with only 6 mu and input prices going up every year, I have to watch what I spend.

Irrigation — I'll water three times: once before winter so the wheat doesn't freeze out, once in spring at jointing when it needs it, and once during grain fill if it doesn't rain. Pumping from the well costs money, the electric meter runs fast. If we get good rain I skip one, save the money.

Herbicide yes — one spray in spring for weeds, otherwise the weeds take over. No way around it.

**Then maize, right after wheat harvest.** This is the tight part. Wheat off around June 10th, maize in the ground within a week. No time to plow properly. I hire the neighbor with the no-till planter — he does my 6 mu in a morning for about 40 yuan per mu. Worth it. No way I can do it by hand in that heat.

Maize seed is hybrid, I have to buy new every year — about 60 yuan per mu for decent seed. I put compound fertilizer down at planting and topdress urea at big trumpet stage. A bit less nitrogen than wheat — maize doesn't need quite as much and it's cheaper that way.

Irrigation for maize depends on the rain. Usually one or two waterings. Summer rain here is unpredictable.

Labor — my wife and I do most of it. My son works in the city, he sends money but doesn't come back for farming anymore. For harvest we hire the combine for both wheat and maize, no choice, no young people to cut by hand. I also do some work at the market in the off season so I have a little extra cash.

My goal this year — same as every year. Get about 450 kg of wheat per mu and maybe 500 kg of maize per mu. That's what I usually get. Grain prices haven't moved much, so I'm not changing much.
